nodes.description: De novo heterozygous deletion reported as arr[hg19] 6p22.3 (19849280-21604600)x1 in the 2015 series. These are the outermost deleted probes; Table 2 gives flanking normal probes at chr6:19840492 and chr6:21630684. The approximately 1.76 Mb minimum interval removes MBOAT1, E2F3, CDKAL1 and SOX4, including coding, intronic and intervening intergenic sequence, but leaves the proposed target ID4 intact. The deletion and its de novo origin were confirmed by qPCR.

nodes.description: Heterozygous deletion reported as arr[hg19] 6p22.3 (19974194-22013061)x1 in the 2015 series. These coordinates are the outermost deleted probes, not nucleotide-resolved breakpoints; Table 2 gives flanking normal probes at chr6:19965294 and chr6:22016585. The interval removes MBOAT1, E2F3, CDKAL1 and SOX4, including coding, intronic and intervening intergenic sequence, while retaining ID4. ID4 is the proposed regulatory target, not a deleted coding gene. Parental samples were unavailable, so origin is unconfirmed for this allele despite the abstract's collective de novo wording.

nodes.description: De novo inversion identified by whole-genome sequencing after a negative array in the 2026 report. The author-deposited LOVD record gives the hg38 genomic description on chromosome 6 as g.19066060_21763046delins[CGAATTAACTGT;19066051_21763045inv]. Supplementary Figure 2 documents a templated insertion at the telomeric breakpoint, so this is not represented as a completely balanced simple inversion. ID4 is a predicted regulatory target whose coding sequence is retained. Genomic contexts are omitted because the accessed abstract and supplement do not establish transcript-specific breakpoint overlaps.

evidence.snippet: we predict that the structural variant disrupts several topologically associated domains (TADs) in the region and is likely to place ID4 in closer proximity to more telomerically located limb enhancers, which could result in enhancer adoption and potentially lead to ID4 limb misexpression

nodes.description: Both allele classes are predicted to disrupt topologically associating domains at 6p22.3 and place ID4 nearer to limb enhancers that normally cannot reach it. ID4 is an inhibitor-of-DNA-binding HLH protein — a dominant-negative regulator of bHLH transcription factors — so misexpressing it in the limb bud would be expected to interfere with, rather than augment, the differentiation programs those factors run. Both papers state this as a prediction from breakpoint position, not as a measured expression change.

evidence.reference_title: Microdeletions on 6p22.3 are associated with mesomelic dysplasia Savarirayan type.
evidence.snippet: We identified a fourth patient with intellectual disability and an overlapping slightly larger do novo deletion also encompassing the flanking gene ID4. Given the fact that the fourth patient had no skeletal abnormalities and none of the genes in the deleted interval are known to be associated with abnormalities in skeletal development, other mutational mechanisms than loss of function of the deleted genes have to be considered.

evidence.reference_title: Microdeletions on 6p22.3 are associated with mesomelic dysplasia Savarirayan type.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the genomic region showed that the deletion removes two regulatory boundaries and brings several potential limb enhancers into close proximity of ID4. Thus, the deletion could result in the aberrant activation and misexpression of ID4 in the limb bud, thereby causing the mesomelic dysplasia.
